title: Pulling a Catering Order off the Kitchen List
content:
## The subject

A client under a Corporate Catering Service Agreement is pulling one of its catering orders. What this governs is the value recorded against that order at the moment notice is given, in USD.

## What the registration does

A cancellation entry is written into the agreement's order history against the order reference given, stamped with today as the day notice was given, and carrying the guest count the order stood on, the day it was to have been served and the value it held at that moment. The kitchen stops work on it, and the client sees the order struck from the agreement with that value recorded against it.

## Invoking the tool

The tool is `register_order_cancellation_69ffeeb0`. It belongs to the client rather than to the desk: the desk unlocks it and hands it over, and it is the customer themselves who runs it to pull their own order.

## Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `catering_agreement_id` | the reference number of the corporate catering service agreement the order sits under | an identifier, as the desk reads it off the client's agreement record |
| `customer_id` | the reference number of the client organisation profile the agreement belongs to | an identifier, as the desk reads it off the client's dining profile |
| `order_reference` | the catering order being pulled, written as the order reference it carries throughout its history | CO- followed by 6 digits |
| `service_date` | the day the catering was to have been served, in the site's own calendar | YYYY-MM-DD; never left empty |
| `headcount` | the guest count the order stood on when it was pulled | a whole number of guests, an integer with no decimal part, never left empty |
| `order_channel` | the route by which this cancellation instruction reached Larkspur Table, which is a fact about how the client passed the instruction on rather than about the medium of any one conversation | one of four values, set out below |
| `standing_order_value_usd` | the value the order held at the moment notice was given | USD to 2 decimal places, rounded half to even at the point it is booked and never carried to a finer precision; no time zone applies and it is never left empty |

### The four values `order_channel` takes

- `online_portal` — the client entered the instruction themselves in the client ordering portal.
- `account_manager` — the client gave the instruction to the named catering account manager looking after them rather than to the client services desk.
- `phone` — the client spoke the instruction to the client services desk on the telephone and passed it through no one else.
- `email` — the client sent the instruction in writing to the desk's mailbox.

## What comes back

A confirmation sentence naming the cancellation reference the entry was filed under, the order reference pulled, the day notice was given written as YYYY-MM-DD and the value recorded in USD to two decimal places. The presence of the cancellation reference is what indicates the cancellation was registered; afterwards the order history shows one further cancellation entry against that order.
